title: Ang 773–774: the Lavan
tomorrow: what does faithful really look like? Guru Amar Das has a hard answer

cards: Wedding videos love the big moments: the entrance, the first dance, the cake. At an Anand Karaj, a Sikh wedding, the center is quieter.

The couple walk around the Guru Granth Sahib, the groom ahead and the bride following, while the Lavan are sung: four stanzas by Guru Ram Das on ang 773 and 774, one round for each. So what does each round mean?

teach.h: FIRST: THE WORK OF A HOUSEHOLD.
teach.b: In paraphrase. The first round: the Lord sets out the work of a household life; hold to the Guru's word and to right living, and remember the Name.
The second: the True Guru is met; in awe of God the mind becomes fearless, and the dirt of ego washes away.
The third: the mind fills with longing for the Lord, a love that lets go. The fourth: the mind comes to ease, sahaj, and the Lord is found. Hear what that does to a wedding.
It's the couple's day, and the Lavan picture two lives and the One, step by step: duty, fearlessness, longing, ease.

teach.h: THE WEEK WALKED RIGHT UP TO IT.
teach.b: And this week walked right up to it. Three voices, one ending. Union, the friend who walks with you.
Guarded, a hand over the head. The bride, the color that holds. Skill in love, simply being there.
The friend is home. Suhi has been rehearsing this all week.

games.q: your cousin, married a few months, says the glow has worn off: now it's chores and bills. she wonders if something went wrong. what fits the Lavan?
o: maybe it did; a good marriage should keep its first glow.
the first round is the household's work; it was there from the start.
chores aren't spiritual; save that side for the gurdwara.
games.why: the Lavan's first round sets out the work of a household life, before fearlessness, longing and ease. the chores are part of the walk.

practice: Say the four rounds out loud, slowly, one word for each breath: duty, fearless, longing, ease. Then go around once more in silence, and let the last one, ease, stay with you for the sit.

wordCard.voice: Ang 773. Where the Lavan begin: Guru Ram Das's four rounds, sung as a Sikh couple walks around the Granth.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: laav, a round; har pahilarhee laav, the first round (ang 773). The four together are the Lavan.

carryVoice: Four rounds: duty, fearlessness, longing, ease, walked one step at a time. Fifteen-forty, and the week comes full circle.
